title: Execution follows fenced resident memory
summary: The cluster moves compact ooRexx runner/object continuation state to the Memory Fabric provider that already owns the required working set. Queue Fabric carries durable object/control envelopes over a protected XTP named-service route; resident memory is not pulled merely because execution moves.
invariants: Application objects remain ordinary ooRexx objects and contain no node, Queue Fabric or XTP policy.
Memory Fabric owns block/provider identity, block generation, provider owner epoch and residency.
Job-to-Node owns hard execution eligibility, admission, ranking and placement leases.
Queue Fabric owns transmission queues, receiver ACL/security-domain checks, idempotent acceptTransfer and durable transfer receipts.
XTP owns protected named-service carrier selection and key/session protection; XTP packet ACK, DIAG, ECHO or session establishment is not Queue Fabric durable acceptance.
A cluster MOVE carries a fenced memory reference and compact runner state, not resident PCM, decoded media, tensor or other bulk working data.
A MOVE provider_id must map to the selected peer route before the Queue Fabric transmission queue is touched.
Queue Fabric may ACK its local transmission package only after an authenticated durable remote receipt.
cluster.object.peer/0.2 releases the old source object generation only after the destination MOVE response confirms the next generation.
Any missing route, stale provider mapping, failed readiness evidence, ambiguous transport or absent reply becomes MOVE_UNCERTAIN and leaves the source generation resident.
Live XTP movement is default-denied until an injected authoritative route-readiness check is backed by current selected-route and field evidence.
